cliff.title: The income cliff
cliff.description: This shows the estimated yearly help your household could get as income rises. Above the 60% State Median Income line, most of it drops away at once.
cliff.chartAriaLabel: Chart of estimated yearly energy help versus household income, with the 60% State Median Income cliff marked
cliff.estimateNote: Dollar figures are estimates and shown as ranges elsewhere. Your local agency decides eligibility.

aboveCliff.heading: Your income looks above the 60% SMI cliff
aboveCliff.body: The main chain may not apply, but these programs may still help. Call the Heatline to be sure.
aboveCliff.belowBody: You look below the cliff, so the linked chain may be available to you.

good_neighbor.name: Good Neighbor Energy Fund
good_neighbor.next_step: Call 2-1-1 or the Heatline to reach your local Salvation Army office.

oil_relief.name: Middle-Income Heating Oil Relief
oil_relief.next_step: Applications open in December 2026. Call the Heatline to ask how to apply.

abovecliff.ask: Call the Heatline to ask what help is available for your household.

result.title: Your energy help, step by step
result.subtitle: Here's what may be available to you, and where to start. This is a guide, not a decision.
result.disclaimer: Heat Path is a screener, not legal advice or an eligibility decision. Your local agency and utility make the final decision on your eligibility.
result.chainIntro: These programs build on each other. Start at the top.
result.protectionsIntro: If you may be protected from a shutoff, here's what to say when you call.

program.prior_winter_heap_presumption: You may already be protected from HEAP last winter
program.elderly_with_minor: Protection for seniors raising a child

unlock.income_at_or_below_60_smi: Your income looks within the limit

heap.next_step: Apply for HEAP through your local Community Action Agency. Call the Heatline to find yours.
heap.above_cliff: Your income looks above the HEAP limit. Call the Heatline to check, since not all income counts.

amp.next_step: Once you have the discount, ask your utility to enroll you in the Arrearage Management Program to work down past-due debt.
amp.mlp: Ask your light plant whether they offer a debt-forgiveness or payment-plan program.

mass_save.next_step: Call Mass Save about no-cost income-eligible upgrades like insulation and heating equipment.
mass_save.mlp: Ask your light plant about their energy-efficiency programs.

discount.enroll: Ask your utility to put you on the income-eligible discount rate.
discount.lost: Your income looks above the discount limit. Call the Heatline to be sure.

mlp.ask_light_plant: Discount rates work differently for town and city light plants. Ask your light plant what they offer.

unknown.check_bill: Check the top of your bill for your utility's name, then ask them about the income-eligible discount rate.

pending.ask_utility: This utility's discount is being updated. Ask your utility what rate you may qualify for.

billcheck.heading: Check your rate
billcheck.retroactive: You may be owed money if you were on the standard rate while eligible for the discount. Contact your HEAP agency or legal aid.

moratorium.script: Call your utility and say you want winter shutoff protection. Ask for the financial hardship form and return it within 7 days.

heap_presumption.script: Call your utility to confirm they have you protected from getting HEAP last winter, and apply for HEAP again before January 1. Don't assume it's handled — call to confirm.

infant.script: Call your utility and tell them a baby under 1 lives in your home. You can start by phone, then send a document (like a birth certificate) within 7 days.

illness.script: Have a doctor, nurse practitioner, or board of health official call your utility about the serious illness, then send the certificate within 7 days.

elderly_minor.script: Call your utility and tell them all adults in the home are 65 or older and a child lives there. Ask for shutoff protection.

all_65.script: Call your utility and tell them everyone in the home is 65 or older. They can't shut you off without DPU approval, and you can name someone to get copies of notices.
